title: Generative artificial intelligence-driven adaptive learning for sustainable, personalized, and resilient education systems
venue: International Journal of Applied Resilience and Sustainability
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of how generative artificial intelligence can be used to make education more personalized, scalable, resilient, and sustainable. The authors argue that traditional educational systems struggle to meet diverse learner needs, support individualized pacing, and remain effective under disruption, while also raising concerns about equity, privacy, and pedagogical fit. To examine this problem, they conduct a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of recent work on generative AI in education, with emphasis on developments from 2023 onward.

The paper synthesizes literature on generative AI tools such as large language models, multimodal systems, intelligent tutoring agents, and adaptive learning platforms. It discusses applications including personalized content generation, real-time feedback, automated assessment, curriculum sequencing, pedagogical agents, and simulation-based learning. The review also considers implementation methods such as prompt engineering, fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, learner modeling, real-time adaptation, and explainability features, alongside pedagogical frameworks like constructivism, sociocultural learning, cognitive load management, and universal design for learning.

The context spans K-12 education as well as higher education, professional development, and lifelong learning, but the paper is not an empirical intervention study with a specific participant sample. Its main conclusion is that generative AI offers substantial promise for personalized and resilient learning systems, while also creating important risks related to algorithmic bias, privacy, digital inequity, hallucinations, and weak pedagogical integration. The authors emphasize hybrid human-AI models, continuous monitoring, and careful governance as the most promising directions for future educational implementation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative/systematic literature review rather than an empirical evaluation, and it does not report original study design, effect estimation, or K-12 authentic teacher planning/coaching cycle evidence. Although it cites PRISMA, the paper is primarily conceptual synthesis and grey-literature style discussion of generative AI applications.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues for potentially broad educational benefits, but it provides no direct causal evidence or effect sizes from K-12 settings. The likely impact is therefore unclear and only modestly informative for the target research question about authentic teacher planning and coaching cycles.

interventions.use_case: Generative AI tutoring and conversational educational agents used for personalized explanations, open-ended dialogue, misconception remediation, and adaptive feedback in K-12 and other learning contexts.
AI-driven adaptive learning systems that personalize content, difficulty, pacing, curriculum sequencing, and learning pathways based on learner models and performance signals.
Generative AI systems providing real-time personalized feedback on student work, including essay feedback, math misconception feedback, and formative assessment responses.
Language-learning and writing-support applications using generative AI for grammar correction, pronunciation feedback, conversational practice, and multilingual content generation.
Generative AI-created scenario-based simulations and role-play environments for business, medical, and history learning, enabling practice in dynamic risk-free contexts.
